findings: The Windows Paper loopback run used the real supervisor and authenticated console flow. Deploy, pause, resume, rollback, failed replacement restoration, and stop all reached their expected operation states.
The structured lifecycle record explicitly reports venue_worker_started=false, orders_sent=false, and external_network_access=false.

The SQLite restart run verifies the durable terminal state after supervisor restart: desired revision 4, desired_running=false, observation phase=stopped. The failed replacement reports restoration of the prior revision.
The lifecycle evidence validator accepts the recorded backend/environment and enforces the expected operation sequence and stopped state.

A Windows local PostgreSQL 18.6 run also passed the complete distributed/transactional Paper deployment lifecycle, including failed replacement restoration and durable stop; the backend-aware lifecycle evidence validator passes.

The extended Windows SQLite Paper lifecycle completed a clean supervisor stop through stdin EOF and restarted with a different strategy worker PID; the Python checkpoint was supplied, roundtripped, and observed by one restore callback.
limitations: This is isolated Paper loopback acceptance; it does not provide full live readiness, account/venue reconciliation, or live authorization.
Linux lifecycle CI and authoritative live readiness/venue authorization remain pending.
